'''Virtual Set 1: Legacy''' is the first of the [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)|numbered Virtual Sets]] produced by the [[Players Committee]]. Its twelve cards became tournament-legal on 9 March 2002. The early sheets call it ''Virtual Set #1'' or ''Virtual Set #1a''; the later PC-remastered sheet uses ''Virtual Set 1: Legacy''.<ref name="vs1a" /><ref name="ia" />

The virtual cards are paper slips used with their underlying [[Premiere]] cards. Players print and cut out the area beneath a virtual card's title, then sleeve it with the original card, leaving its uncovered information and icons visible. The early instructions use [[Luke Skywalker]] as the example and recommend opaque sleeves.<ref name="vs1a" />

The early layouts, [[#Premium Edition|Premium Edition]] and PC remaster are documented below. The card list pairs the PC-remastered slips with full-card reconstructions made for the wiki in 2026; the historical publication articles remain linked through Versions.

== Publication history ==
=== Announcement and launch ===
On 12 February 2002, TheForce.net reported that the first Virtual Set was planned for release on 4 March through Decipher's website, following a preview week scheduled for 25 February–1 March. The new text was intended to complement [[Premiere]], with further Virtual Sets planned at three- to four-month intervals.<ref name="announce">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Players_Committee_Announces_the_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68946.asp Player's Committee Announces the First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.net (12 February 2002).</ref>

A first card spoiler was reported on 20 February, ahead of that preview week.<ref name="spoiler">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/First_Virtual_Card_Spoiler_Released_68849.asp First Virtual Card Spoiler Released], TheForce.net (20 February 2002).</ref> Decipher's launch announcement, dated 5 March, explained that the Gameplay Design team had selected Premiere cards regarded as obsolete or of little use and given them new text to strengthen their tournament use and storyline play. The set contained six cards for each side of the Force.<ref name="launch">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020610072829/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/playerscommittee/virtualcardset1.html Virtual Card Set #1 is Away!], [[Josh Radke]], [[Decipher]] (5 March 2002); capture 10 June 2002, 07:28:29 UTC.</ref>

Players could choose original or Virtual text while constructing a deck, and could include both versions, but could not switch a card's text after a tournament began. The cards became legal on 9 March; sanctioned tournaments were required to allow them.<ref name="launch" />

The [[Game Players Network]] marked the debut with a deck-building contest reported on 5 March. Entries using the new cards were accepted through 31 March; the winning Light Side and Dark Side decks were each offered an uncut [[Reflections III]] sheet for their side.<ref name="contest">[https://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Deck_Contest_Commemorates_the_Debut_of_First_Virtual_Card_Set_68615.asp Deck Contest Commemorates the Debut of First Virtual Card Set], TheForce.net (5 March 2002).</ref>

=== Early slips and print options ===
The early ''Virtual Set #1a'' sheet has unnumbered lower-card cutouts, with Dark Side text printed white on black. The numbered ''Virtual Set #1'' printout adds V1 collector labels. Both carry the same 9 March 2002 tournament-legality notice.<ref name="vs1a" /><ref name="numbered">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050813215254/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/virtual/VirtualCards1.pdf Virtual Set #1], [[Players Committee]], distributed through [[Decipher]], p. 1, numbered slip layout and printed 9 March 2002 legality notice.</ref>

The early layouts preserve the same [[Darth Vader (V) (Virtual Set 1: Legacy) (Original unnumbered)|Darth Vader]] pilot bonus of 4 and once-per-battle destiny subtraction of 3.<ref name="vs1a" /><ref name="numbered" />

=== Decipher.com distribution ===
On 11 June 2002, [[Decipher]]'s Star Wars CCG card-list index included a separate Players Committee Virtual Card Sets section above the expansion lists. It listed the twelve-card first set and its tournament-legality date, explained how to sleeve the printable text with original cards, and offered black-border and white-border downloads. ''Set #1a'' was offered alongside ''Set #1'' as the Dark Side white-on-black text option.<ref name="legal">[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611031545/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG card lists], [[Decipher]], preserved 11 June 2002, Players Committee Virtual Card Sets section.</ref>

The four download targets were under Decipher's own <code>/starwars/cardlists/virtual/</code> path: <code>VirtualCards1.pdf</code>, <code>ULVirtualCards1.pdf</code>, <code>VirtualCards1a.pdf</code> and <code>ULVirtualCards1a.pdf</code>. The index also linked to a separate first-set information page.<ref name="legal" />

The 2 October 2002 capture of the corresponding <code>www.decipher.com</code> index omits both the Virtual-card introduction and the Players Committee Virtual Card Sets section; its product table starts with [[Theed Palace]].<ref name="removed">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021002220730/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG card lists], [[Decipher]], capture 2 October 2002, 22:07:30 UTC.</ref>

By 6 November 2002, the [[Players Committee]] website listed Set #1 on its own Virtual Cards download page, linking to <code>www.theforce.net/ccg/vcards/VirtualCards1a.pdf</code>.<ref name="pcdownloads">[https://web.archive.org/web/20021106220953/http://www.swccgpc.com/virtualcards.htm Virtual Cards!], [[Players Committee]], capture 6 November 2002, 22:09:53 UTC.</ref>

=== Numbered Dark Side print options ===
The numbered sheets offer two presentations of the same text and numerical values: black-on-white in Set #1 and white-on-black in Set #1a. Their Light Side slips retain the same presentation. Decipher offered them together as print choices.<ref name="legal" /><ref name="numbered" /><ref name="numbered1a">[https://web.archive.org/web/20070117223920/http://decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/virtual/VirtualCards1a.pdf Virtual Set #1a], [[Players Committee]], numbered Decipher-hosted sheet, p. 1; capture 17 January 2007, 22:39:20 UTC.</ref>

The original files are available as [[Media:Decipher-Virtual-Set-1-numbered.pdf|numbered Set #1 PDF]] and [[Media:Decipher-Virtual-Set-1a-numbered.pdf|numbered Set #1a PDF]].

=== Premium Edition ===
'''Premium Edition''' presents the same twelve underlying cards as a one-page sheet of lower-card slips with production-style frames, printed statistics, card types and collector marks. Its footer reads “SWCCG Player’s Committee 2002”; the PDF records creation on 3 February 2005. Those are a printed footer year and a file-creation timestamp, respectively.<ref name="vs1p">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualCards1Premium.pdf Virtual Set #1 Premium Edition], [[Players Committee]], p. 1, title, slips, printing instructions and icon key; footer year 2002, PDF creation metadata 3 February 2005. Wiki original: [[Media:VirtualCards1Premium.pdf|download PDF]]; [[:File:VirtualCards1Premium.pdf|file provenance]]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008193754/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualCards1Premium.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

The sheet's icon key abbreviates recurring rules text. A Pilot marker followed by a number supplies the corresponding piloting power bonus and a [[Pilot]] icon; ▲ takes a card into hand from Reserve Deck, and ▼ deploys it from Reserve Deck, with reshuffling in each case. Crossed-out Alter, Control and Sense markers indicate the corresponding immunity. The slips retain this shorthand in their individual articles.<ref name="vs1p" />

For example, [[Luke Skywalker (V) (Virtual Set 1: Legacy) (Premium)|Premium Luke Skywalker]] prints the piloting bonus as a Pilot marker and a separate [[Attack Run]] sentence. [[Darth Vader (V) (Virtual Set 1: Legacy) (Premium)|Premium Darth Vader]] retains the early 4-point piloting bonus and 3-point destiny subtraction, using the same marker.<ref name="vs1p" />

The [[Media:VirtualCards1Premium.pdf|original Premium Edition PDF]] is available with its [[:File:VirtualCards1Premium.pdf|source and file provenance]]. All twelve Premium card articles are linked in the [[#Slip editions and versions|edition comparison]].<ref name="vs1p" />

=== PC-remastered Legacy sheet ===
The later two-page sheet is titled ''Virtual Set 1: Legacy'' and prints an official-text cutoff of 4 December 2006. Its PDF records creation on 5 December 2006. The first page contains the ''Legacy'' pack illustration, set symbol, expanded icon key, printing instructions, and separate proofing and graphic-design team credits; the second page contains the twelve slips.<ref name="ia" />

This edition includes wording revisions as well as presentation changes. [[Darth Vader (V) (Virtual Set 1: Legacy) (Remastered 2006)|Darth Vader's PC-remastered slip]] replaces the early once-per-battle wording with “During battle” and adds “cumulatively” to its destiny-subtraction clause. The piloting bonus remains 4 and the subtraction remains 3.<ref name="ia" />

=== Later-era versions ===
The later [[Darth Vader (V) (Virtual Block 1)|Virtual Block 1 Darth Vader]] uses a piloting bonus of 3 and destiny subtraction of 2. These differ from both the early and PC-remastered Original-era slips.<ref name="block1">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf Virtual Block 1], [[Players Committee]], p. 2, Darth Vader (V), slip 07E; printed official-text date 7 December 2009. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020181626/https://res.starwarsccg.org/legacyblocks/VirtualBlock1.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> The comparisons below link the Original-era publications separately from their [[Virtual Legacy]] and [[Virtual Modern]] successors.
